journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on dental education: Benefits, challenges, and future directions – A systematic review of the literature
abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental education is a profound opportunity, spurred on by unprecedented technological change. It should be revamped in a way that supports immense capabilities, improves efficiency, and provides learning opportunities, but also has constraints that need to be understood. Thus, in this article, we discuss the benefits and challenges involved in adapting AI into dental education, as well as methods to improve the application of AI to enhance learning for students and instructors. We reviewed a total of 73 articles from multiple databases, including PubMed/Medline, Cochrane, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Through our review of articles from the past five years (2018–2024), the selected studies were evaluated based on relevance, recency, and credibility, which were sometimes difficult to distinguish between. We ultimately found 56 articles that met the above criteria for relevance. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Disparities in educational service quality among medical students in Iran’s revised medical curriculum: A cross-sectional study in a resource-limited region
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ongoing evaluation of educational service quality in medical schools is essential, particularly in settings with limited resources. This study assessed the discrepancy between expected and perceived educational service quality among medical students in the Sistan region of Iran. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional analytical study involved 195 medical students enrolled in the revised curriculum at Zabol University of Medical Sciences. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the SERVQUAL instrument, which measures the quality of educational services. Statistical analyses included paired t -tests, independent t -tests, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). RESULTS: Significant negative gaps were found across all dimensions of educational service quality. The smallest discrepancy was identified in the tangibles domain, while the reliability domain showed the most significant gap. Non-local students reported greater dissatisfaction in the tangibles domain. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Health-related quality of life among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus using EuroQol five-dimension five level: A cross-sectional study from an urban health training center, Coimbatore, India
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus significantly impacts health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Data from urban primary care settings in South India remain limited. This study assessed HRQoL among type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients and identified demographic and clinical determinants associated with EuroQol five-dimension five level (EQ-5D-5L) index and EQ visual analogue scale (EQ-VAS) scores. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted (April–July 2025) at the urban health training center (UHTC), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India. A total of 279 T2DM patients (aged ≥18 years) were enrolled using consecutive sampling. HRQoL was assessed using the licensed Tamil and English EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Data were analyzed using R software; Chi-square tests and independent t -tests were applied ( P RESULTS: Mean EQ-5D-5L index was 0.63 ± 0.37 and EQ-VAS was 72.6 ± 18.0. Pain/discomfort (52.1%) and anxiety/depression (43.2%) were the most affected dimensions. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Exploring the convergence of faith healing practices with biopsychosocial interventions for mental health: A qualitative study among faith healers in Madhya Pradesh, India
abstract: BACKGROUND: Faith healing, a practice deeply rooted in cultural and religious beliefs, remains a significant healthcare approach worldwide, especially in regions like India, where mental health stigma is pervasive. Despite advances in psychiatric care, many individuals still seek the services of faith healers for mental health issues, delaying access to appropriate medical treatment. The study aims to understand the perspectives of Faith Healers on mental health, examine their practices and beliefs, and explore the feasibility of integrating faith healing with psychiatric care to enhance mental health outcomes in Madhya Pradesh. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted across selected districts of Madhya Pradesh, India. The participants were Faith Healers’ who were interviewed by Psychiatrists from “Mankaksh” (District Mental Health Units) between July 2022 and February 2023. In-depth interviews (IDIs) were conducted with 24 faith healers using a predefined interview guide. These IDIs were later analyzed. Thematic analysis was used to identify key themes from the data. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Impact of burden of care upon psychological wellbeing and quality of life among family caregivers for cancer patients
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer is a serious and fatal disease that affects both the patients themselves and their families. This study aimed to investigate the impact of caregiving burden on the quality of life and mental health of family caregivers of cancer patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This research is a cross-sectional study that further investigates family caregivers for their patients with cancer at babel oncology Center in Babylon, Iraq, from September 2025 to February 2026. A purposive sampling method that was applied to a group of 150 patients. Information was gathered through self-report questionnaire. SPSS version 26 was utilized to analyze the data. RESULTS: The results showed that 73.3% of caregivers had a poor caregiving burden and 24.7% had a moderate caregiving burden, with approximately 74% having a fair quality of life, while 52.7% of caregivers had a good level of psychological well-being. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Enhancing public awareness: Insights from mothers and healthcare experts on postpartum depression – A qualitative study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pregnancy and early motherhood represent periods of significant psychological vulnerability. An estimated 10–15% of mothers experience postpartum depression (PPD) annually in India. Maternal mental health (MMH) represents a critical public health concern, impacting both maternal and child well-being. This study constitutes the first qualitative exploration in India to examine perspectives of both mothers and healthcare professionals regarding PPD for the development of culturally appropriate educational intervention. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative exploratory study, conducted from April to August 2023, employed three focus group discussions among a total of 25 participants: 14 mothers attending immunization clinics at urban and rural primary health centres, and 11 healthcare professionals with expertise in MMH. Semi-structured discussion guides facilitated exploration of PPD awareness, cultural beliefs, barriers, and intervention preferences. Audio recordings were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using thematic analysis. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates
abstract: BACKGROUND: Burnout is a growing concern among healthcare professionals (HCPs) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Emerging evidence suggests that sleep quality and spiritual well-being may buffer against burnout and enhance professional fulfilment. This study explores the relationship between sleep disturbance, spiritual well-being, and burnout among HCPs in the UAE. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 661 healthcare professionals across the UAE. Validated instruments were used to measure sleep quality, circadian regularity, spiritual well-being, burnout, and professional fulfilment. Data was analyzed using correlation and regression models to identify predictive factors. RESULTS: Poor sleep quality and irregular circadian patterns were significantly associated with higher levels of burnout. Conversely, higher spiritual well-being showed a strong negative correlation with burnout and a positive association with professional fulfilment. Multivariate analysis identified sleep regularity and spiritual well-being as significant independent predictors of both burnout and professional fulfilment. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Inflammatory indices and bone density in osteoporosis: A cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis and osteopenia, prevalent metabolic bone disorders, increase fracture risk, particularly in postmenopausal women. Chronic inflammation may contribute to bone loss. The association between inflammatory indices and bone mineral density (BMD) was investigated. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis involving 99 patients over the age of 40 at the Ilam Rheumatology Clinic (2019–2022) evaluated BMD using the Hologic Discovery Wi DXA and assessed blood indices with the Sysmex XN-1000. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: The impact of helicopter teaching in nursing education and approaches to foster independent learning: A narrative review
abstract: The ‘helicopter teaching’ in nursing education can be harmful to the development of clinical judgement, decision-making, and autonomy among nursing students because it involves excessive control, constant supervision, and over-dependence. This narrative review examines the impact of helicopter teaching on the academic and professional development of nursing students. It also discusses evidence-based approaches that encourage independent learning and resilience. We searched databases such as PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus with a mixture of search terms and Medical Subject Headings to analyze the evidence between 2010 and 2024. The review identified several contributing factors behind this helicopter style of teaching including faculty anxiety, a lack of confidence in student competency, and institutional pressures relating to patient safety. The study also examined how such practices can negatively impact student learning and these include reduced confidence, limited thinking and dependence on instructors. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: A neuroeducational approach to STEM education: Integrating real-time cognitive analysis and cognitive load theory to optimize teaching and learning at universities
abstract: BACKGROUND: The relevance of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education to effectively meet challenging academic requirements has become imperative for university entrants. With emerging advancements within the domain of learning neuroscience and analytics, it has become possible to analyze and track the real-time mental states of learners. This has opened several avenues to apply the theoretical perspectives of Cognitive Load Theory (CLT). Though applications of neuro-technological interventions for learning have become widely sought, their effective implementation within STEM education has not been comprehensive at the university level. The innovations brought about within this study include its conceptual fusion for STEM education based upon real-time mental state analysis and CLT. The goal of this research is to integrate the current research findings on real-time cognitive analysis practices used in STEM education in universities and analyze how cognitive load can be monitored dynamically and discuss teaching practices according to principles of CLT to improve effectiveness and inclusiveness for better cognitive load management throughout learning. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Pedagogical determinants of cognitive flexibility among pre-service school counselors in Indonesia: A multisite cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: School counselors are mental-health service providers for students, working in complex and unpredictable situations that demand rapid adaptive responding. Cognitive flexibility is the core adaptive skill for this work, but how counselor education can cultivate cognitive flexibility in pre-service school counselors is still not well established. This study aims to investigate the association between the levels of cognitive flexibility and the pedagogical quality of counseling courses that have been implemented in counselor education programs in Indonesia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 846 pre-service school counselors who had completed theoretical and practical counseling courses under supervision were recruited in this multisite cross-sectional survey study (M Age = 21.44, SD = 2.64). The respondents in our study came from 21 universities in Indonesia. An ordinal logistic regression model was used for statistical analysis. RESULTS: The study found that (a) the scores of theoretical and practical counseling courses under supervisors, (b) students’ ratings of their practical counseling course skills, (c) learning materials, (d) learning models, and (e) evaluation lear

journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Effects of an online stroke education program on enhancing knowledge, awareness of stroke warning signs, and emergency medical services seeking among high-risk residents in Huanggang City, China
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is the leading cause of disability and death in china. Raising public awareness of warning signs is critical for improving access to emergency services and treatment outcomes. Prehospital delay remains a significant challenge, especially among high-risk populations. This study therefore aims to determine the effects of an online stroke education program (osp) on the knowledge, awareness of stroke warning signs, and seeking of emergency medical services (ems) among high-risk residents. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted from September 2024 to April 2025. One hundred and six high-risk residents were randomly allocated to intervention and control groups ( n = 53 each). The intervention group received the 6-week OSP program, while the control group received regular health education. Data were collected via an interview questionnaire and analyzed using the Chi-squared test, McNemar’s test, and multivariate regression. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Role of digital health interventions in strengthening human resources for primary healthcare systems in India: A systematic review
abstract: Inlow- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like India, Human Resources for Health (HRH) constitute the backbone of a health system, providing critical services to ensure equitable, accessible, and high-quality healthcare for all. However, they are often overburdened, which hinders their performance and impact. The digital health interventions can appear as a boon to assist and enhance the performance of HRH, thereby delivering better healthcare services. To evaluate the impact and the effectiveness of digital health interventions on healthcare workforce capacity building in primary health care settings in India. A systematic review of published research was conducted as per the PRISMA guidelines. Online databases (PubMed and Google Scholar) were explored to identify studies written in English from January 2015 to March 2025 that discuss digital health interventions within Primary Healthcare settings or involve human resources in those settings in the Indian context. The review included all forms of messaging, voice calls, and interactive voice responses as interventions. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Enhancing first-aid self-efficacy: A randomized trial comparing three interactive educational ınterventions
abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective first-aid education is a critical public health strategy to reduce the burden on emergency services. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of three interactive first-aid training modalities (case-, video-, and drama-based) on university students’ first-aid self-efficacy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A three-arm randomized controlled trial with a pretest–post-test design was conducted. The study included 93 university students, randomly assigned to three intervention groups ( n = 31 each). The intervention groups received six core first-aid topics delivered through case-, video-, or drama-based methods, while the control group received unstructured education. Data were collected using the “First Aid Self-Efficacy Scale.” Statistical analysis was performed using analysis of covariance to compare post-test scores while controlling for baseline differences. RESULTS: More than 95% of the participants were unmarried, and more than 50% in each study group were female. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Efficacy of ginger and fennel in relieving primary dysmenorrhea: A triple-blind crossover controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary dysmenorrhea, characterized by painful menstrual cramps without underlying pelvic pathology, is common among young women and affects physical and emotional wellbeing. This study was conducted to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of ginger and fennel in relieving primary dysmenorrhea. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A triple-blind crossover clinical trial was conducted from October 2020 to March 2022 at one medical college and two schools in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India, among 384 young women aged 18–26 years. Participants received ginger (500 mg), fennel (480 mg) or placebo capsules every 8 h during the first three days of menstruation for three cycles, with washout periods between interventions. Pain severity, intensity and duration were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Short Form McGill Pain Questionnaire and self-reported pain duration. Data analysis was performed using repeated measures ANOVA and paired t-tests in SPSS version 27, with a significance level set at P RESULTS: A total of 384 participants (mean age: 20.66 ± 1.66 years) completed the study. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Examination of students’ perspectives regarding the effectiveness of clinical training: A research endeavor congruent with social responsibility
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical education is a fundamental component of medical training. This study examines the experiences of clinical students across various health professions to provide valuable insights for educational planners involved in designing effective and socially relevant clinical training curricula. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This descriptive-analytical study employed a stratified random sampling method to select clinical students from the disciplines of nursing, midwifery, operating room technology, and pre-hospital emergency medicine at educational institutions in Shoushtar. Data were gathered using a standardized questionnaire designed to evaluate factors affecting the quality of clinical education. The data were analyzed using Pearson correlation, Chi-square tests, independent t-tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA). RESULTS: A total of 190 students participated in the study, including 60 males and 130 females, with ages ranging from 18 to 39 years. Participants were enrolled in nursing ( n = 105), operating room technology ( n = 30), midwifery ( n = 40), and emergency medicine ( n = 15) programs. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: A digital–spiritual assistance Dzikry model to improve hemoglobin levels and antenatal care compliance: A quasi-experimental study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal anemia remains a significant contributor to adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Although universal health insurance has expanded access to antenatal care (ANC), coverage alone does not guarantee optimal utilization. Innovative approaches addressing behavioral, cultural, and motivational factors are needed. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a digital–spiritual assistance Dzikry model in improving maternal hemoglobin status and ANC compliance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasiexperimental nonequivalent control group design with pretest–posttest measurements were conducted among 60 second-trimester pregnant women at a clinic in Tangerang, Indonesia. Participants were allocated to an intervention group receiving digital education, visit reminders, and spiritually oriented motivational support, or a control group receiving standard ANC services. Hemoglobin levels were measured at baseline and follow-up. Secondary outcomes included ANC compliance, maternal knowledge, and perceived communication quality. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Global perspectives on health tourism: A comparative review of research trends and future prospects (2000–2024)
abstract: This study systematically reviews global research trends in health tourism (2000–2024), comparing international and Chinese scholarly perspectives to identify key themes, differences, and future directions for the field. We employed a systematic literature analysis approach, examining studies on health tourism definitions, classifications, motivations, influencing factors, evaluation systems, and development strategies. Comparative insights were drawn between international and Chinese research priorities. Findings reveal distinct research emphases: International scholars focus on global perspectives, interdisciplinary integration, cross-border service delivery, and ethical concerns, while Chinese researchers prioritize localized frameworks, regional characteristics, and policy applications. Both groups, however, share an interest in industrial integration and growth drivers. The study recommends that China enhance standardized evaluation methods, deepen quantitative research, and cultivate distinctive health tourism brands. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Transforming lupus self-care education with mobile health: A systematic review
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic, multisystemic, autoimmune, and inflammatory disease with complex and variable phenotypes and clinical presentations. Patients with SLE often experience low self-esteem, a fear of death, and difficulty in being understood by family and friends. One effective approach to managing and combating SLE is the use of mobile health (mHealth). This study aims to explore the role of mHealth in educating SLE patients on self-care. This systematic review, conducted in August 2024 and updated in February 2025, involved searches in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using the keywords “Mobile Health,” “Lupus,” and “Self-care.” Studies published in English that utilized mHealth to educate SLE patients on self-care were deemed eligible for inclusion. Titles and abstracts were independently reviewed based on the inclusion criteria, and full-text articles were subsequently obtained and reviewed according to the eligibility requirements. A total of 10 studies that met the inclusion criteria were included in the systematic review. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Fear of childbirth and its relationship with the attitude toward child bearing: A descriptive-analytical study
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: With regard to the importance of fear of childbirth, negative consequences, its impact on fertility, and the differences in the prevalence and related factors in different regions of Iran, this study was conducted with the aim of determining the status of fear of childbirth and its relationship with attitudes toward fertility in women of childbearing age in the city of Kermanshah. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This descriptive-analytical study was conducted on 600 married women referring to comprehensive health service centers in Kermanshah. The sampling method was multistage random sampling. The data collection tools included a demographic profile form, a questionnaire on childbirth expectations and experiences/attitudes toward fertility and childbearing, which were completed by the participants. The data were analyzed using statistical tests. FINDINGS: The overall prevalence of fear of childbirth is 69.055%, and its subgroups are classified as mild (0.33), moderate (17.30), severe (66.83), and clinical (2.67) based on the fear of childbirth questionnaire scores in this study. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Design and validation of a multisensory game-based tooth brushing education tool for children with visual and hearing impairment
abstract: BACKGROUND: Children with sensory disabilities exhibit a poor oral hygiene and a high prevalence of gingivitis and dental caries. Tailored multisensory oral health education interventions may improve tooth brushing skills and oral health. To develop and validate a multisensory game-based educational intervention to teach tooth brushing to children with visual and hearing impairments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A developmental research design was used. A prototype was developed after literature review and expert interviews. This was validated by dentists and special educators and field tested among 15 children with visual impairment and 15 with hearing impairment with 7 play sessions over 4 weeks. Comprehensibility and acceptability were assessed through structured feedback, and effectiveness was measured by evaluating tooth brushing skills. RESULTS: Experts agreed with the relevance, sequential accuracy of the brushing technique, and clarity of the game (Item-level Content Validity Index (I-CVI) and k* =1.00), confirming excellent content validity. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Sawdust–plaster cast mixture versus traditional cast: Which type reduced pain and increases comfort and enhancing healing process among patients with twisting: A randomized controlled clinical trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal twisting injuries, such as strains and sprains, are common and can be treated using cast immobilization without the need for surgery. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of Sawdust–Plaster Cast Mixture Versus Traditional Cast: Which Type Reduced Pain and Increases Comfort and Enhancing the healing process among Patients with Twisting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted from May to August 2025 and used a single-blind, true experimental design. Sixty patients with twisting injuries were randomly assigned to either the intervention group ( n = 29), which received the sawdust–plaster cast, or the control group ( n = 31), which received a standard cast. Pain and comfort levels were assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS), and the healing duration was recorded. Statistical analysis was performed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 30. RESULTS: Compared to the standard cast (control) group, patients in the sawdust–plaster cast mixture (intervention) group reported a noticeably higher reduction in discomfort. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Comparing the pain relief effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate and ketorolac versus intravenous morphine and ketorolac for kidney stones
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pain is one of the most common symptoms in various diseases. While morphine is widely used for pain relief, its adverse effects and potential for misuse have led to the exploration of safer alternatives. This study aimed to compare the analgesic effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate versus morphine, both in combination with ketorolac, in patients with renal colic. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this double-blind randomized controlled trial, 174 patients with renal colic referred to the emergency department of Shahid Ganjiyan Hospital in Dezful were enrolled. Patients were randomly allocated into two equal groups ( n = 87). The intervention group received intravenous magnesium sulfate (50 mg/kg diluted in 100 mL normal saline over 15 minutes) plus ketorolac (30 mg), while the control group received intravenous morphine (0.1 mg/kg) plus ketorolac (30 mg). Pain intensity was measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline (admission), and 20, 40, and 60 minutes after drug administration. Demographic data were also collected. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Impact of music therapy on diabetes distress and bio-physiological parameters in patients with diabetic foot ulcer
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common and significant complication of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (DM), frequently resulting in increased physiological suffering and emotional burden. Music therapy, as a complementary intervention, has shown potential in lowering stress and improving general well-being, but its influence on patients with DFU is unknown. The present study aimed to identify the impact of music therapy on diabetes distress and bio-physiological parameters among patients with DFU. METHODS AND MATERIALS: The study was conducted in a selected tertiary care hospital in South India, and a Quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group research design was used. A non-probability purposive sampling was used to select 159 participants with DFU into three groups: Group I (n = 53) received patient-selected music therapy, Group II (n = 53) received researcher-selected music, and the control group (n = 53) received routine treatment only. The intervention involved listening to music for 20 minutes twice daily over 21 consecutive days, along with standard medical care. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Navigating the PhD thesis journey: A qualitative study of doctoral students and supervisors at a medical university in Iran
abstract: BACKGROUND: The PhD thesis serves as a cornerstone of doctoral education, yet it is often accompanied by considerable stress and inefficiencies for both students and supervisors. Although global research has extensively addressed issues such as supervision quality, institutional support, and student well-being, there is limited investigation into these dynamics from a qualitative perspective in non-Western academic settings. This study examines the lived experiences of doctoral students and their supervisors at Isfahan University of Medical Sciences to identify challenges and propose tailored reforms for this specific context. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Employing a qualitative exploratory design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 54 participants (31 PhD students and 23 faculty supervisors) chosen through purposive sampling. The collected data underwent conventional content analysis, with themes integrated across both groups to form a unified framework. RESULTS: The analysis revealed five overarching themes and 21 associated categories, including supervisory competencies, administrative ambiguity, resource limitations, psychological stress, and the importance of early resea

journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: The impact of group cognitive behavioral therapy on stress and psychological adjustment among cigarette, e-cigarette, and hookah smokers
abstract: BACKGROUND: The tobacco epidemic remains one of the world’s major public health threats, causing preventable cancers and disabilities, and claiming over seven million lives each year. Over the past decade, the use of nicotine-containing electronic cigarettes has grown among adolescents and young adults. This study investigates the effectiveness of a group cognitive behavioral therapy program on stress and psychological adjustment among university students who want to quit smoking cigarettes or hookah. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The sample included 123 male students who smoked cigarettes and e-cigarettes and 134 students who smoked hookah, all of whom expressed a desire to quit smoking. Students who smoke both cigarettes and hookah were excluded from the study to ensure clear differentiation between the two groups of users. A nonprobability sampling method was used. Psychological stress and psychological adjustments were measured twice: before the group treatment program began and after the program was completed. The study employed an experimental pretest and posttest design to analyze data. RESULTS: The results indicated that the program had an effective impact on users of cigarettes,

journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Impact of oil fortification with iron in the prevention of anemia—A systematic review
abstract: Micronutrient malnutrition has gained its significant influence on public health and a role in the worldwide disease burden in recent years. Through fortification, the nutritional profile of staple foods is enhanced, making them more nutritious and beneficial for consumption. This systematic review aims to assess the impact of oil fortification with iron in anemia prevention. Electronic search through five databases and additional resources was performed by using the appropriate keywords. Out of 13,948 records that were identified, one double-blind randomized controlled trial done among Swiss women met eligibility criteria. Selected study focused on women aged between 18 and 40 years with low serum ferritin, evaluating the impact of iron-fortified low-fat margarine. This study is registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023420044). Intervention showed an increase in body iron stores with both compounds, namely, sodium iron ethylenediaminetetraacetate (NaFeEDTA) and micronized ground ferric pyrophosphate (MGFePP); however, NaFeEDTA fortification demonstrated a two to three times greater impact compared to MGFePP fortification. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Determinant factors of sexual and reproductive health literacy among adolescents in Indonesia: A national population-based study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual and reproductive health literacy (SRHL) among adolescents is a global public health concern. Almost half of all new cases of sexually transmitted infections have been associated with health literacy among youth. Limited SRHL has led to negative behaviours and their impact on health-related outcomes. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to identify the determinants of SRHL among adolescents in Indonesia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study drew on the most recent nationwide, population-based cross-sectional study and applied Nutbeam’s functional health literacy framework. SRHL was determined as a composite index and classified into three levels: limited, inadequate, and adequate. Pearson’s Chi-square test was used to determine the different proportions of SRHL. Binary logistic regression with a complex survey design was used to evaluate the factors associated with SRHL. The crude and adjusted odds ratios (AOR) along with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported. RESULTS: The magnitude of adequate literacy was 32.69% (95% CI, 31.92%–33.45%). journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: The relationship between health literacy and the adoption of preventive behaviors against high blood pressure among villagers: A cross-sectional study in Iran
abstract: BACKGROUND: Considering the limited number of studies on health literacy among the rural population, the necessity of measuring the level of health literacy, and the increasing number of patients with hypertension, the present study aimed to determine the relationship between health literacy and the adoption of preventive behaviors in high blood pressure among the villagers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a descriptive-analytical cross-sectional study, 300 villagers living in Qayenat were selected by multi-stage random sampling in 2024. The data were obtained by demographic and background characteristics and the health literacy assessment questionnaire (HELIA) as well as a valid and reliable questionnaire to measure the adoption of preventive behaviors against hypertension. The data were analyzed using SPSS ver 22. (IBM Coporation, Armonk, NY) and descriptive statistics and logistic regression. title: Effectiveness of video-enhanced educational intervention for fluid management on knowledge, practice, and adherence among patients undergoing hemodialysis: A randomized controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluid management remains a cornerstone of hemodialysis care; however, suboptimal adherence frequently precipitates life-threatening complications, including hypertension and cardiovascular morbidity. While educational interventions are essential to mitigate these risks, empirical evidence regarding the efficacy of video-enhanced instruction in this population remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a structured video-enhanced educational intervention on knowledge, practice, and fluid adherence among patients undergoing hemodialysis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This randomized controlled trial evaluated outcomes using a knowledge questionnaire (reliability 0.88), a practice checklist (0.79), and intradialytic weight gain (IDWG) in 128 hemodialysis patients at South Indian tertiary hospital. title: Prediction of phase angle based on body composition: Insights from a large population-based registry
abstract: BACKGROUND: Phase angle (PhA) is obtained through bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) and is a potential marker of nutritional health and cellular function. We aimed to develop an equation for estimating PhA using body composition parameters, focusing on skeletal muscle mass, body water, and fat mass. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled participants from the Iranian National Obesity Registry. Data on age, gender, body composition, and BIA measurements were collected using an InBody 770 device. Exclusion criteria included pregnancy, pacemakers, implants, or edema. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Mashhad University of Medical Sciences. RESULTS: A total of 5980 participants (28.7% men, 71.3% women) were included. PhA showed the strongest correlations with extracellular water/total body water (ECW/TBW) ( r = −0.84, P r = 0.62, P r = 0.62, P P P R ² = 0.75), and SMM (β = 0.039, P R ² = 0.85). Including body fat mass (BFM) (β = 0.005, P P R ² = 0.90). CONCLUSION: ECW/TBW, SMM, BFM, age, and height are significant predictors of PhA, with ECW/TBW showing the strongest negative association.

title: Differential effects of unilateral forced nostril breathing on baroreflex sensitivity and cardiovascular parameters in healthy young men: A cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Baroreflex sensitivity (BRS) is a crucial marker of autonomic cardiovascular control, and it is also a predictor of cardiovascular risk. Unilateral forced nostril breathing (UFNB) is one of the many types of pranayama, which are breathing techniques in Yoga. This type of breathing can influence autonomic function through hemispheric activation, yet its direct impact on BRS remains unexplored. To assess the immediate effects of left and right UFNB on BRS and cardiovascular parameters in healthy young adult men. MATERIALS AND METHODS: It is a cross-section study, which included 55 healthy adult men (mean age 25.67 ± 5.89 years). The participants underwent the standardized protocols for measuring BRS, blood pressure, and heart rate during baseline and the 2-minute interventions of left and right UFNB. BRS was measured using the sequence method with Finapres technology. Paired t -tests were used to compare the baseline and the postintervention values. title: Design and implementation of a pediatric failure to thrive registry system in Iran
abstract: BACKGROUND: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to inadequate growth caused by an inability to acquire or use enough calories for growth. It refers to a failure to develop over time, which can lead to more serious problems in adulthood if left untreated. FTT is a significant global health concern, particularly in developing countries like Iran. Effective FTT management necessitates timely, inclusive, and precise data on children’s FTT status. A pediatric FTT registry system is a useful tool for gathering and managing data on children with FTT. This study proposes a pediatric FTT registry system for Iran. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A developmental-applied study was conducted in three phases during 2024. The first phase involved defining the features of a pediatric FTT registry system through interviews with experts. The second phase entailed expert validation using the Delphi method. In the third phase, the software was designed based on a conceptual model using the Hypertext Preprocessor programming language and the Laravel framework. title: Telenutrition health education program to increase nutritional awareness, attitude, and dietary diversity among secondary high school adolescent girls in rural area of Bangladesh: A quasi-experimental study protocol
abstract: BACKGROUND: Telenutrition, using telehealth technologies for remote nutritional care, has proven effective in primary care. Nutritional deficiencies constitute a global health burden, characterized by chronic undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies, especially in adolescent girls in impoverished nations such as Bangladesh. Telenutrition, which uses digital technologies to provide remote nutritional treatment, is a promising strategy to decrease this burden. This study aims to determine the impact of telenutrition education on improving nutritional awareness, attitude, and dietary diversity among school going adolescent girls in rural Bangladesh. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A school-based quasi-experimental study was conducted among 190 adolescent girls (95 intervention, 95 control) from two higher secondary schools in Sakhipur, Bangladesh. Schools were allocated into intervention and control groups using a coin toss method to reduce selection bias and to mitigate the risk of contamination of health education information among students within the same school. title: Artificial intelligence and its impact on oral health care education. A randomized study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated educational materials demonstrate superior effectiveness in improving patient comprehension and reducing anxiety compared to traditional methods. Their integration into dental practice could enhance patient satisfaction and streamline the educational process, particularly for complex or anxiety-inducing procedures. The present study aimed to evaluate the act of AI applications on oral healthcare, focusing on clinical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cluster-randomized controlled trial with 1000 participants from 20 villages (10 interventions, 10 controls) was conducted. The intervention group received 4 weeks of chatbot-guided oral health education via WhatsApp/IVR, while controls received standard health talks and leaflets. Knowledge, oral hygiene practices, and OHI-S scores were measured pre- and post-intervention. title: Health behavior and hygiene practices among islamic boarding school students in Indonesia: A qualitative study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Islamic boarding schools in Indonesia are essential for religious and character education, yet health behavior and hygiene practices (HBHP) among students remain limited, leading to preventable illnesses. This study aimed to explore HBHP in boarding schools, identify supporting and inhibiting factors, and examine the role of community health centers (CHCs) in promoting student health. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A qualitative design with thematic analysis was applied. Nineteen informants were purposively selected, including students, teachers, administrators, caretakers, CHC health promotion officers, and a health department representative. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and participatory observation and then analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s framework with NVivo 12 Plus. RESULTS: Five themes emerged: (1) daily hygiene constraints and common health disorders such as skin, digestive, and respiratory problems; (2) psychosocial and academic impacts of illness, including homesickness, reduced concentration, and disrupted religious activities; (3) factors shaping health behavior, including institutional rules, role models, peer influence, and personal habits; (4)

title: Investigating the effect of vitamin C supplementation on bacterial vaginosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Bacterial vaginosis (BV), the most common type of vaginitis, results from reduced vaginal lactobacilli and increased anaerobic bacteria. Vitamin C may aid BV treatment by promoting lactic acid production. This study evaluated the effectiveness of vitamin C in treating BV. To this aim, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Iranian databases identified randomized clinical trials published up to October 29, 2024. The protocol for this systematic review is registered. Risk of bias was assessed using the Verhagen tool. Mean differences and their 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the random-effects model. The quality of the evidence was evaluated with GRADEpro Guideline Development Tool, and statistical analyses were conducted using Review Manager (RevMan v5.3). Substantial heterogeneity (I 2 >50%) prompted the use of the random-effects model, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses to investigate its origins. The meta-analysis included six randomized controlled trials of varying quality. title: Localizing the main components of competencies in high-level managers based on health system evaluation indicators: Content analysis approach
abstract: BACKGROUND: Managers play a key role in organizations. Competence of managers has become an important issue for organizations. This issue is very important for high-level managers in health-oriented organizations. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to identify and determine the components and analyze the core competencies of high-level managers in the field of health in medical sciences universities of the country, with the approach of content analysis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted using the content analysis method in 2023-2024. Data collection included retrieving documents from relevant databases. The studied population was high-level managers in the field of health promotion (presidents, vice presidents, university professors, and experienced human resource managers). For this purpose, semi-structured interviews were conducted with managers. The purposeful sampling method was chosen, and finally, the sampling was continued until the saturation time. title: The effect of self-study training on resilience and effective coping style of women involved in domestic violence
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a serious yet preventable public health issue. Resilience plays a significant role in helping women overcome the effects of IPV. The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of self-help training on the resilience of women exposed to IPV. MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this clinical trial, 62 female survivors of violence who were attending comprehensive health service centers in 2022, randomly assigned to either an intervention or a control group. Data collection instruments included a demographic characteristics questionnaire, the Violence Against Women Scale, the Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), and the problem-focused coping subscale of the Ways of Coping Questionnaire (WOCQ) by Lazarus and Folkman. The training in this study was delivered in person using lectures, group discussions, and question-and-answer sessions. The total number of sessions was 14 sessions of 60 min each, for two groups of 16 participants. Data were analyzed using SPSS software (version 21), independent t -tests, and analysis of variance with repeated measures (ANOVA).
